eligibility.reference: Raine R, Wallace I, Nic a' Bháird C, et al. (2014). Improving the effectiveness of multidisciplinary team meetings for patients with chronic diseases: a prospective observational study. Health Services and Delivery Research 2(37). doi:10.3310/hsdr02370
eligibility.reason: Relationships among professionals and between team and patients in NHS MDT meetings; reports Q and N findings.

decisions.reason: Weekly MDT meetings of 12 NHS chronic disease teams (relations among professionals and between team and patients); regression on 2512 patients, TCI, panel ratings (N) and thematic analysis of 370 meetings and 73 interviews (Q).

Findings as reported, with page references and quotes. F46 kept as the Q output of the analytic conferences (p.76); F47, F49, F50, F52, F54, F55 are panel ratings, new N data (rule 13); F51 and F53 are Q from the consensus meeting transcript.
Not a finding: panellists rated level of support only (p.77); no feasibility rating is reported, so the p.80 sentence restates claim C11 without data.
Rule 12: qualitative themes compared across teams grouped by measured implementation rate (F3) or by number of professional groups (F6, F7); F15-F19 root in both strands.
Rules 9 and 13: turning metathemes and quantitative results into 68 statements is instrument development, a design-level interface point for the notes, not a transformation of findings.
Rule 13: panel ratings of the statements are new N data, not transformations of F46; the study 1 to study 2 chain is a design-level note.
Rule 6: recommendations for future research, not headline claims.
Rule 6: under 'Future research priorities' (p.88), concerns the design of future interventions; research agenda, not a practice recommendation.
rests_on F48, which is not a finding; replaced by C76 with empty rests_on (no finding in the text).
rests_on wrongly empty: rule 7 (Discussion p.69 states that the highest-implementing teams were the most medically dominated) and rule 8 (same measure as F3, same theme as F21); replaced by C77.
rests_on wrongly empty: rule 7 (Discussion p.73) and rule 8 (F13 gradient in cancer teams, F16 guideline reference); replaced by C78.
Two separable assertions (rule 1), each restating panel results (rules 7, 8: Chapter 6 p.82 and p.85); replaced by C79 (F52, F53) and C80 (F50).

Text check: SS Results p.xxvi-xxvii reports clear goals from the high- vs lower-implementing comparison and then 'Implementation was also more likely in MDTs with a good team climate' (TCI) as a separate sentence; C4 is the qualitative comparison, C5 carries the TCI result.
Claim kept as written; reporting inconsistency noted: Table 12 (F14) gives patient/family choice 15%, below 'other' (28%) and 'reason not given' (21%), so 'commonly' overstates the table.
Claim kept with rests_on F1; inconsistency noted: SS gives median attendees 5-17 and two to six disciplines, Chapter 3 (p.23, Table 7) gives meeting size 5-28 and one to seven groups.
Headline claims with no finding in the text (no mediation analysis; no comparison of teams against the 21 indications); empty rests_on, recorded as unsupported.
Correction rows: C76 (C11 with empty rests_on), C77 and C78 (rules 7, 8), C79 and C80 (rule 1 split of C64, rules 7, 8).

Headline claims from abstract, scientific summary and Chapter 7 (one row per repeated claim, rule 11); rests_on follows rules 2, 3, 7 and 8 (C16 rule 7, Theme 5 p.44-45); judgement and summary claims have empty rests_on. C63, C66-C71 sit under 'Future research priorities' but state results, so rule 6 does not apply.
Covers relations of summary claims (rule 2) stated in the text; R35-R36 marked 'Taken together'.

Rule 10: explicit pointer, Chapter 6 p.82 'our findings illustrate that there is scope for learning between specialties' after the 31% strong-agreement result.
